about: Kit tools: Scenario MCP tools that lay Scenario results out as a walkable world, a game or a film. Each runs scenario_unreal.recipes in the editor's Python (Content/Python). kind: read, editor or change. undo: run inside one undo step (false for tools that open a level or start a render).

tools.name: build_world
tools.description: Creates and opens a new walkable level under /Game/Scenario/Worlds: sun, sky light and fog for the time of day (mist for ground fog), a ground, invisible walls around the play area, a player start and the project's third-person game mode. Generate the Scenario assets first or in parallel; pass them here or to dress_world. Fails if the open level has unsaved changes.

name.description: World name, also the level name ("Misty Bamboo Temple").

size_m.description: Side of the square play area in meters (40 to 600). Default 120: about a minute to walk across.

ground_material.description: Material from a Scenario material result (created_assets path). Tiled in world space.

ground_tile_m.description: Meters per texture tile on the ground. Default 4.

sky.description: Material or panorama texture from a Scenario environment (skybox) result.

game_mode.description: Blueprint game mode path. Default auto: the project's Third Person, First Person or Top Down template game mode.

mist.description: Ground fog from 0 (clear air, default) to 1 (dense). Above 0 the fog is volumetric: light shafts and lantern glow show in it. 0.6 to 0.9 for a misty scene.

tools.name: dress_world
tools.description: Lays Scenario 3D results out on a world made by build_world: a landmark at the center (faces the player start), an optional paved path from the player start to it, props with spacing (lining the path, crossing it as gates, or scattered) kept off the path, plus ground material, sky, mist and looping ambient sound. Meshes are scaled to height_m and rest on the ground. With a sky, the sun is aimed from the sun in the panorama when it shows a clear one (the result's sun says which). Call again with replace true to redo the layout.

landmark.description: The hero object at the center: what the player walks to and the film circles.

mesh.description: Static mesh path (or its import folder).

front_yaw.description: Degrees added so the mesh's front faces the player. Default -90: Scenario 3D models (glTF) face +Y. Try 90, 0 or 180 if it faces away.

path.description: A flat paved strip from the player start to the landmark (or the world's center), in a world-aligned material. Props stay off it.

material.description: Material from a Scenario material result (stone, gravel, planks).

tint.description: [r, g, b] 0 to 1, multiplies the color.

props.description: One entry per Scenario mesh. 300 props at most in total.

height_m.description: Height in meters, or [min, max] for variety. Default 1.5.

area.description: path_sides lines both sides of the path, evenly spaced (lanterns, fences). on_path puts gates and arches across the path so the player walks through them (torii): the widest side crosses the path, and a single gate marks the start of the path. Default anywhere.

yaw.description: "random" (default), "face_center" or degrees. on_path sets its own.

front_yaw.description: Degrees added to face_center (default -90, as for the landmark) or to on_path (default 0).

light.description: true, or {temperature_k (2200), intensity_cd (4), radius_m (4.5), height (0.63 of the prop's height)}: a warm point light inside each placed prop (lanterns, braziers). 48 lights at most per world.

sink_m.description: Sinks the prop into the ground (rocks, roots). Default 0.

ground_tint.description: [r, g, b] 0 to 1, multiplies the ground's color (the ground_material given, or the one already on the ground).

mist.description: Ground fog from 0 to 1, as in build_world. Omit to keep the level's.

ambient.description: Sound from a Scenario audio result, looped over the whole world.

seed.description: Change it for another layout. Default 7.

replace.description: Removes the props, their lights and the landmark of the previous call first. Default true. A new path always replaces the old one.

tools.name: make_game
tools.description: Turns the open level (a kit world or a dressed template) into a small game: Scenario pickups spread over free floor (they spin and glow), an optional goal (in front of the landmark when there is one), a timer, looping music and a HUD. Winning: collect every pickup, then reach the goal. Uses the plugin's Scenario Pickup, Goal and Game Rules actors, so the game also works in a packaged build.

sound.description: Short Scenario sound played on pickup.

goal.description: Omit for a game won by collecting everything.

mesh.description: Optional mesh (portal, shrine, boat). Without it the goal is a glow.

time_limit_s.description: 0: no limit. Default 25 s per pickup plus 30.

objective.description: One HUD line. Default: "Collect every <name>, then reach the goal."

accent.description: HUD and glow color, [r, g, b] 0 to 1.

replace.description: Removes the previous game's actors first. Default true.

tools.name: dress_template
tools.description: Copies an Epic template level of this project (third_person, platforming, combat, first_person, shooter, horror) to /Game/Scenario/Games and dresses the copy with Scenario assets: floor and block materials (world-aligned), meshes swapped for template ones (boxes, cubes, cylinders) at the same size, decor props on free floor, sky and music. The template's gameplay stays. Fails if the open level has unsaved changes.

template.description: A name above or a level path. Default platforming.

floor_material.description: Replaces the grey grid floors and walls.

replace.description: boxes (breakable crates in combat), cubes, cylinders, or a mesh path.

tools.name: make_film
tools.description: Builds a short film in the open level as a Level Sequence: cine cameras on smooth moves (aerial, crane_down, orbit, walk, detail, rise) around the landmark, camera cuts, fade in and out, and Scenario music and sound effects. Default: six shots over duration_s. Then render_film.

music.description: Scenario music for the whole film.

focus.description: What the film is about: an actor label, or [x, y, z] in meters. Default: the landmark.
Actor label or [x, y, z] meters for this shot.

tools.name: render_film
tools.description: Renders a film with Movie Render Queue in the editor, then encodes an MP4 with its music when ffmpeg is installed. Returns at once: poll film_status about every 20 seconds. A 24 s film at 720p draft takes a few minutes.

film.description: Film name or sequence path. Default: the newest film.

quality.description: high: 4 temporal samples (smoother, about 4x slower). Default draft.

tools.name: film_status
tools.description: Where a film render is: rendering (frames_done of frames), encoding, done (mp4 path) or failed (error).

tools.name: kit_status
tools.description: What the kit made in the open level: kit world or not, size, props and their lights, landmark, path, sky, time of day, mist, pickups, goal, game rules, films. During Play it reports the player character instead (pawn, pawn_at_m); stop Play to read the level again.

tools.name: play_level
tools.description: Starts (or stops) Play in the editor so the person can walk the level or play the game. Call kit_status a few seconds after starting: it reports the player character once it has spawned.
